title: Which network for which kind of data
hook: Feed-forward, convolutional, recurrent, transformer, autoencoder, and generators.
inPlainWords: Different data have different shapes. Images have neighbors, sentences have order, and tables have columns. Each network family is built around one of those shapes.

useCase.title: Five kinds of ShopEase data
useCase.story: Order tables, product photos, customer reviews, delivery sensor readings over time, and warehouse audio alarms. Which network family suits each?

approaches.name: Feed-forward network
approaches.what: Layers of simple units, each one seeing all of the inputs.
approaches.greatWhen: Tables and small tasks. It is also the building block inside other networks.
approaches.avoidWhen: Images and long text. There are too many connections and no sense of position.
approaches.example: Predict from one row of numbers.

approaches.name: Convolutional network (CNN)
approaches.what: Slides small filters across an image to find edges, then shapes, then objects.
approaches.example: Detect a cracked screen in a photo.

approaches.name: Recurrent network (RNN, LSTM)
approaches.what: Reads items in order and carries a memory forward.
approaches.greatWhen: Short sequences on small devices, and older systems.
approaches.avoidWhen: Long text. Transformers have replaced most of its uses.
approaches.example: Predict the next reading from a short sensor stream.

approaches.name: Transformer
approaches.what: Looks at all parts of the input at once and learns which parts matter to each other.
approaches.greatWhen: Text, and now images, audio and code. It is the basis of language models.

approaches.name: Autoencoder
approaches.what: Squeezes data into a small summary and rebuilds it. A bad rebuild signals something odd.
approaches.greatWhen: Anomaly detection and cleaning up noise.
approaches.avoidWhen: You have plenty of labeled defects. Classify instead.
approaches.example: Flag a sensor pattern that rebuilds poorly.

approaches.name: Generative models (diffusion, GANs)
approaches.what: Create new images, audio or other data.

challenge.question: Photos on a packing line must be checked for damage in real time. Which family?

options.text: A feed-forward network on raw pixel numbers
options.why: It ignores which pixels are neighbors, so it needs huge data and learns poorly.

options.text: A convolutional or vision transformer network, ideally pretrained
options.why: Built for images, and pretrained versions already know how to see.
It is designed for ordered sequences, not pictures.
Good if you almost have no damaged examples. Otherwise a classifier does better.

bestCase.title: Match the network family to the shape of the data
bestCase.example: Tables get boosted trees or a plain network. Photos get a pretrained convolutional or vision transformer network. Reviews get a transformer. Sensor streams get a small sequence model, or an autoencoder to spot odd patterns. Sound is turned into a picture and given to a convolutional network.

worstCase.title: One favorite network for every problem
worstCase.example: The team pushes photos through a table-style network by flattening the pixels into one long row. It learns nothing about neighbors, needs huge data, and mislabels a slightly shifted photo.

takeaway: Choose the network by the shape of your data. Most modern work reuses a pretrained transformer or convolutional network.
